steps.title: Prepare Strep‑Tag II binding buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 8 g NaCl (136.893 mM), 0.2 g KCl (2.683 mM), 1.44 g Na₂HPO₄ (10.144 mM) and 0.245 g KH₂PO₄ (1.8 mM) in distilled water, adjust to 0.8 L, set pH 7.4 with HCl or NaOH, bring to 1 L with distilled water, filter through a 0.45 µm filter, degas with a vacuum filtration unit and store ≤1 month at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Strep‑Tag II elution buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 8 g NaCl (136.893 mM), 0.2 g KCl (2.683 mM), 1.44 g Na₂HPO₄ (10.144 mM), 0.245 g KH₂PO₄ (1.8 mM), 0.53 g d‑desthiobiotin (2.5 mM) and 0.29 g EDTA (1 mM) in distilled water, adjust to 0.8 L, set pH 7.4 with HCl or NaOH, bring to 1 L with distilled water, filter through a 0.45 µm filter, degas with a vacuum filtration unit and store ≤1 month at 4 °C.

steps.title: Transform plasmids into SHuffle T7
steps.instruction: Introduce the nanobody plasmids (cAbLys3 or H04, His‑tag or Strep‑Tag II versions; Addgene #248353, 248574‑76) into chemically‑competent E. coli SHuffle T7 cells, plate on selective LB agar, and incubate overnight at 37 °C to obtain colonies with confirmed transformation efficiency.

steps.title: Grow culture and induce expression
steps.instruction: Inoculate a single colony into LB medium containing the appropriate antibiotic, grow at 37 °C with shaking until OD₆₀₀ ≈0.6–0.8, add IPTG (concentration as per vector guidelines), shift temperature to 28 °C and incubate for 24 h to allow cytoplasmic expression of disulfide‑bonded nanobodies; expected yields range from 0.1 to 8.4 mg L⁻¹.

steps.title: Harvest cells and lyse protease‑free
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the culture to pellet cells, resuspend the pellet in lysis buffer (protease‑free), and lyse by sonication or homogenization while keeping the sample on ice; maintain protease‑free conditions throughout.

steps.title: Clarify lysate and perform affinity chromatography
steps.instruction: Spin the lysate to remove debris, then load the clarified supernatant onto the appropriate affinity column (Ni‑NTA for His‑tagged proteins or Strep‑Tactin for Strep‑Tag II proteins) equilibrated with the binding buffer prepared in step 1; wash with binding buffer and elute with the elution buffer from step 2.

steps.title: Collect monomeric fractions
steps.instruction: For H04‑His, collect only the monomeric peak (the dimeric form does not bind lysozyme); for H04‑Strep‑Tag II, collect both monomeric and multimeric peaks for later SPR analysis as described in the original study.

steps.title: Size exclusion chromatography (SEC)
steps.instruction: Load the affinity‑purified protein onto a calibrated SEC column, run in appropriate buffer, and collect fractions corresponding to the monomeric peak; note that SEC was used before SDS‑PAGE, western blot, and LC‑MS/MS verification.

steps.title: Validate protein identity and purity
steps.instruction: Analyze SEC fractions by SDS‑PAGE, confirm identity by western blot, and optionally verify sequence by LC‑MS/MS (Support Protocol 1).

steps.title: Prepare SPR running buffer and samples
steps.instruction: Prepare the SPR running buffer (same composition as binding buffer unless otherwise specified), exchange nanobody samples into this buffer, and keep on ice; buffer preparation follows the same steps as in step 1.

steps.title: Immobilize lysozyme on SPR chip
steps.instruction: Activate a CM5 (or equivalent) sensor chip by standard amine coupling, inject HEWL (lysozyme) at the concentration optimized for 20 %–76 % surface activity, block remaining active groups, and confirm immobilization level; all nanobody analytes will be measured on this single ligand surface.

steps.title: Run SPR binding assay
steps.instruction: Inject each nanobody variant (cAbLys3‑His, cAbLys3‑Strep, H04‑His, H04‑Strep) over the lysozyme surface at multiple concentrations, record sensograms (typical run 19 h overnight), and ensure quality checks are passed for each trace.

steps.title: Analyze kinetic data
steps.instruction: Fit association and dissociation phases to obtain kinetic constants (k_on, k_off) and equilibrium dissociation constants (K_D) in the nanomolar range; note that H04 shows a slower dissociation rate than cAbLys3, and surface activity values reflect typical amine coupling efficiency.
